drivers: Meta (-7%) set the tone: revenue beat, but it raised the floor of 2026 capex to $135-145B, posted negative $2.1B free cash flow, and approved a new non-voting Class C share class to fund AI. Its credit-default swaps hit a record. Semis followed: Philly Semi index -5.6% to its lowest since late July (about 25% off the June peak), AMD -8%, Lam Research -10%, Nvidia -4.4%, CoreWeave -10%.

Oil at 5-month highs (WTI ~$99, Brent $113): Iran claimed seven tankers were hit in the Strait of Hormuz overnight, Houthi drones struck Saudi Arabia's Shaybah field and Dammam airport, and a NYT report said the US and Israel have drawn up post-midterm strike plans on Iran. Energy stocks still fell, with oil services down ~5%.

Flight to Treasuries, not gold: yields plunged across the curve (10-yr -16 bp to 4.96%, biggest one-day drop since March 2023; 2-yr -15 bp to 4.65%) even though jobless claims came in at 194K vs 200K expected. Breakevens barely moved, so this was a real-rate/safe-haven move; gold and silver sold off with it.

Rotation, not panic: the majority of stocks rose. Staples +3.3% (P&G rally), utilities +2.1%, health care +1.3%, financials +1.1%; value and small caps beat growth by 1.5-2 points. Spotify and Lockheed rallied on raised guidance; Blackstone +8%. The Dow clawed back a ~300-point early loss to finish unchanged. Session sold off from the open and never reversed.

afterHours.why: Beat ($4.64 vs $4.11 EPS; rev $4.38B vs $4.14B) and guided Q2 well above Street ($5.80 EPS vs $4.84; rev $5.1B vs $4.57B); raised dividend. Muted reaction after a -7% regular session.
Reports after the close; no reaction posted yet.
Does not report tonight; earnings are Oct 29. Fell with the chip group ahead of the print.

briefs.headline: Risk-off: stocks lower, led by chips and AI names, as Tesla, Meta and Lam Research earnings failed to impress and oil pushed toward $100 on Saudi attacks and reports of planned US-Israel strikes on Iran.

data.name: Initial jobless claims (wk 10/17)
data.read: lowest since July; low-fire labor market
data.reaction: futures held ~-1% S&P / -1.6% NDX; 10-yr kept sliding to ~5.05% on risk-off

drivers: AI-trade fatigue: Tesla cut 2026 capex to about $20B from about $25B and fell about 5% pre-market before paring; Meta beat on revenue but booked a roughly $10B legal charge and narrowed capex to $135-145B, shares down about 6% early. Lam Research fell 7-10% on a supply-constrained outlook; SOX -3% with NVDA, AMD, INTC and MRVL all lower.

Oil: Houthi strikes on Saudi oil infrastructure, the State Dept ordering non-emergency staff out of Saudi Arabia, and a NYT report of a short but intensive US-Israel operation against Iran after the midterms. Brent hit a five-month high near $112; WTI near $99.
Rates and Fed: FOMC is in blackout ahead of Oct 27-28; FedWatch prices about 87% odds of a hold, with a December hike widely expected. Yields are falling today on risk-off flows, not on the data.
Overseas: Asia sold off hard (Nikkei -2.7%, Hang Seng -3.0%, KOSPI -3.5%, Taiwan -1.8%); Europe lower (Stoxx 600 -0.6%, CAC -1.3%, DAX -0.5%) after a hot UK CPI print of 3.5%.
